title: Grab and Move with Win key affects other Win-key hotkeys
author: jingyu9575

status.label: Focused fix hypothesis is ready for design approval
status.detail: When Grab and Move uses Win, the first Win-modified key can be swallowed before Keyboard Manager, Command Palette, or SendInput consumers see it; pressing the key a second time while Win remains held works.

next_action.label: Approve the focused fix direction
next_action.reason: The fast judgment identifies a repository change, while implementation-grade design remains deferred.

judgment.rationale: The issue is current, maintainer-reproduced, cross-module, and precise enough to propose coordinating the pending Win activation with unrelated key forwarding.
evidence: Maintainer Chealer reproduced the exact sequence on 0.100.2.
The first 0 press is lost and the second becomes the configured 1.
PR 47326 changed Grab and Move to absorb and replay both Win down and up to avoid an ordering race.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve the focused design direction, then run the full issue-to-design workflow before implementation.

fix_assessment.rationale: No current upstream or fork implementation fully covers the reproduced interaction.

proposed_fixes.title: Forward the first non-mouse Win chord coherently across Grab and Move and other hooks
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Grab and Move's pending Win activation consumes or replays modifier events independently from other low-level keyboard hooks, so the first unrelated Win chord is observed with incomplete ordering.
plan: Instrument Grab and Move and Keyboard Manager hook callbacks for the exact Win+0 sequence and module enable order.
Cancel pending Grab and Move activation on unrelated keyboard input while replaying the complete Win-plus-key sequence before dependent hooks evaluate it.
Avoid recursive handling of replayed events and preserve the mouse-gesture path and Start-menu suppression rules.
Add integration regression coverage for Keyboard Manager and Command Palette Win shortcuts with both module enable orders and after restart.
verification: Run the seven-step maintainer reproduction and confirm the first Win+0 press maps to 1.
Verify Command Palette's Win shortcut and an external SendInput Win chord on the first press.
Verify Win+mouse Grab and Move remains functional and releasing Win does not open Start unexpectedly.

confidence.rationale: The public reproduction and prior hook fixes identify the interaction boundary, but exact event ordering still requires a maintainer trace.

issue_context.summary: When Grab and Move uses Win, the first Win-modified key can be swallowed before Keyboard Manager, Command Palette, or SendInput consumers see it; pressing the key a second time while Win remains held works.
known_information: A maintainer reproduced the issue on 0.100.2.
The report gives a deterministic Keyboard Manager Win+0 mapping and hook-priority setup.
Other commenters confirm effects on Command Palette and Keyboard Manager.
The first non-modifier key is lost while a second press succeeds under the same held Win key.
inferences: Grab and Move likely consumes the first key event to cancel a pending Win activation and replays modifier state too late for another low-level hook to match the same chord.
Hook installation order changes exposure, explaining why disabling and re-enabling modules alters the result.
issue_context.analysis: The deterministic two-module reproduction and prior Win replay fix identify an inter-hook event-ordering defect suitable for focused design, with exact ordering still to be traced.
initial_investigation: Read the complete issue body and all public comments.
Inspected the linked Grab and Move fixes and related issue relationships.
Used the public reproductions to separate confirmed symptoms from the hook-order root-cause hypothesis.

actions.label: Trace first Win chord across module hooks

prerequisites: Enable Grab and Move and select Win as the activation modifier.
Create a Keyboard Manager shortcut mapping Win+0 to the single key 1.
Disable and re-enable Keyboard Manager so its hook priority matches the report.
Open Run and focus its text box.
steps: Hold Win and press 0 once; record Grab and Move and Keyboard Manager hook events and injected flags.
Without releasing Win, press 0 a second time.
Repeat after reversing the module enable order.
Disable Grab and Move and repeat as the control.
reproduce.expected_result: The first Win+0 press is delivered to Keyboard Manager and produces 1 regardless of module enable order, while Grab and Move still activates only for Win+mouse gestures.
